ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, and $BC=4\sqrt{3}$. Point P is a movable point on the right-angled side BC (P does not coincide with B or C). Connect AP and rotate line segment AP clockwise by $60^\circ$ around point A to obtain line segment AD. Connect CD. What is the minimum value of line segment CD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Rotate the line segment AC clockwise by $60^\circ$ around point A to get the line segment AE, and connect DE. Then, as point D moves on DE, when CD$\perp$DE, the value of the line segment CD is minimized. Draw CF$\perp$AE at point F through point C. By the property of rotation: $\triangle AED\cong \triangle ACP$, $\therefore \angle AED=\angle ACP=90^\circ$. Since CD$\perp$DE and CF$\perp$AE, $\therefore$ quadrilateral EDCF is a rectangle, $\therefore$ CD=EF. In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, BC=$4\sqrt{3}$, $\therefore$ AC=$BC\tan30^\circ=4\sqrt{3}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=4$, $\therefore$ AE=AC=4. In $\triangle ACF$, $\angle AFC=90^\circ$, $\angle FAC=60^\circ$, $\therefore$ AF=$AC\times\cos60^\circ=4\times\frac{1}{2}=2$, $\therefore$ EF=AE−AF=4−2=2, $\therefore$ CD=\boxed{2}.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/analytic optimization method. First read the diagram as a right triangle with C at the right-angle corner, CB as the horizontal base to the right, AC vertical upward, and P moving along CB. From the text, compute AC=BC·tan30°=4. Set coordinates C=(0,0), B=(4√3,0), A=(0,4), and let P=(t,0) with 0<t<4√3. Then vector AP=(t,-4). Rotating this vector clockwise by 60° gives (t/2−2√3, −√3t/2−2). Therefore D=A+rotated(AP)=(t/2−2√3, 2−√3t/2). As t varies, D lies on the line y=−√3x−4, with x between −2√3 and 0. The minimum CD is the distance from C=(0,0) to this line, provided the perpendicular foot lies on the allowed segment; the foot is inside the interval. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, and $BC=4\sqrt{3}$. Point $P$ is a movable point on the right-angled side $BC$ ($P$ does not coincide with $B$ or $C$). Connect $AP$ and rotate line segment $AP$ clockwise by $60^\circ$ around point $A$ to obtain line segment $AD$. Connect $CD$. What is the minimum value of line segment $CD$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} Rotate the line segment $AC$ clockwise by $60^\circ$ around point $A$ to get the line segment $AE$, and connect $DE$. Then, as point $D$ moves on $DE$, when $CD\perp DE$, the value of the line segment $CD$ is minimized. Draw $CF\perp AE$ at point $F$ through point $C$. By the property of rotation: $\triangle AED\cong \triangle ACP$, $\therefore \angle AED=\angle ACP=90^\circ$. Since $CD\perp DE$ and $CF\perp AE$, $\therefore$ quadrilateral $EDCF$ is a rectangle, $\therefore CD=EF$. In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, $BC=4\sqrt{3}$, $\therefore AC=BC\tan30^\circ=4\sqrt{3}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}=4$, $\therefore AE=AC=4$. In $\triangle ACF$, $\angle AFC=90^\circ$, $\angle FAC=60^\circ$, $\therefore AF=AC\times\cos60^\circ=4\times\frac{1}{2}=2$, $\therefore EF=AE-AF=4-2=2$, $\therefore CD=\boxed{2}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: Observe the attached figure: A is above, C is directly below A, B is to the right of C, AC is drawn as a vertical line segment, CB is drawn as a horizontal line segment, and there is a right-angle mark at C; P is located on the horizontal line segment CB and between C and B; A is connected to P, and in the figure there is AD obtained by rotating AP clockwise, point D is located near the lower left of C, and CD is also connected in the figure.

Reasoning: It is known that in triangle ABC, ∠ACB=90°, ∠B=30°, BC=4√3. Because tan30°=AC/BC, AC=BC·tan30°=4√3·√3/3=4.

According to the rotation idea, also rotate AC clockwise 60° around A to obtain AE. Since AP is rotated clockwise 60° around A to obtain AD, and at the same time AC is rotated clockwise 60° around A to obtain AE, the line segment CP corresponds to the line segment ED after rotation. Also because CP is on BC, and AC⊥BC, CP⊥AC; rotation preserves the perpendicular relationship, therefore ED⊥AE. Thus when P moves on BC, D moves on the line passing through E and perpendicular to AE.

To make CD minimum, one should take the perpendicular distance from C to this line, that is, it is minimum when CD⊥ED. Draw CF⊥AE through C, with foot F. At this time, because ED⊥AE, CD⊥ED, CF⊥AE, quadrilateral EDCF is a rectangle, so CD=EF.

Rotation preserves length, so AE=AC=4. Also ∠CAE=60°, in right triangle ACF, AF=AC·cos60°=4·1/2=2. Therefore EF=AE−AF=4−2=2. Therefore the minimum value of CD is 2.
